why: An ordinary agent editing or deleting a saved recipe template receives a refusal saying recipe templates can only be used and edited in the GUI. Management refusal is intended, but the use restriction contradicts the supported create --template launch path. The obsolete pending-billing comment and matching test assertion are the same wording defect, not separate findings. This is diagnostic and contract accuracy; no authorization failure or loss of user work is alleged.

A supplied recipe target is refused before approval; existing recipe templates are rejected by find_template, reached by edit and delete. recipe_template_refusal says 'Recipe templates can only be used and edited in Farhelm's GUI' and documents GUI-only use pending billing design. This is a real management-request diagnostic, not merely unused text.

Complete governing sections distinguish management from launch: SPEC.md:1563-1564 limits GUI-only to listing and writing and expressly allows ordinary-host create --template; :4324-4335 permits recipe-target templates through their own Allow/Deny card. SPEC_impl.md:6680 expressly routes a plain hostless create using a recipe template through the environment-launch path. Thus correct management refusal does not make the broader guidance true.

The feature adds the fleet-origin, non-spawn, hostless recipe-template branch to plan and launch an environment using saved templates and known recipes. The management test retains the false wording. The launch test constructs a hostless Create with dev-container and expects LaunchEnvironment plus direct Allow before Deny. These are source and test-oracle checks only; no test was executed.

The exclusive base uses known_recipes: &[] and the feature parent uses the restricted resolver; the feature introduces the supported recipe-template launch path while retaining the message. Attribution is an in-range semantic contradiction introduced by 190d844e, not introduction of the literal.
